companies.latest_signal: Core Local Commerce swung back to a RMB5.7bn operating profit (7.9% margin, +52% YoY) in Q2 2026 as delivery unit economics turned positive for the first time and subsidies were pulled back amid regulator pressure on 'involution' competition; New Initiatives loss narrowed further to RMB1.7bn.

companies.label: Alibaba
companies.metric_name: China e-commerce Group (Taobao & Tmall) adjusted EBITA, YoY change
companies.metric_basis: Alibaba does not disclose a standalone P&L for Taobao Instant Commerce/Taobao Shangou; management explicitly attributes the YoY decline in China e-commerce Group adjusted EBITA to quick-commerce subsidy and user-acquisition investment each quarter, making it the closest disclosed loss proxy

periods.src: Alibaba June Quarter 2026 results; Sina Finance '份额保持、减亏加速，淘宝闪购稳了' (Aug 2026)

companies.latest_signal: Chinese coverage (Sina Finance, Aug 2026) describes Q2 2026 as 'share held, loss-narrowing accelerating' — Taobao Flash Sale/Shangou unit economics improved sequentially faster than expected on higher AOV and fulfillment efficiency, share stabilized near 42%, and the YoY EBITA drag shrank to essentially flat from -76% a year earlier, though S&M spend (RMB47.6bn, 17.7% of revenue) remains elevated against the RMB50bn subsidy pool announced July 2025 that press reported half-spent within one quarter.

companies.label: JD.com
companies.metric_basis: JD's disclosed New Businesses segment operating loss (JD Food Delivery/JD Takeaway, Jingxi, JD Property, overseas); management states the segment's loss trend is driven almost entirely by JD Food Delivery investment, and calls out food-delivery-specific YoY loss reduction on earnings calls without breaking it out as a standalone reported number

periods.src: JD.com Q1 2026 results; management cited >30% QoQ narrowing, largest sequential improvement since segment's creation (Guandian.cn, 36kr)
JD.com Q2 2026 results (6-K); Tencent News/163.com coverage

companies.latest_signal: JD management said on the Q2 2026 call that JD Food Delivery losses narrowed more than 50% YoY while order volume held up, and guided that full-year 2026 total delivery investment will be lower than 2025; New Businesses segment loss has now narrowed for three consecutive quarters (RMB14.8bn to RMB10.35bn to RMB9.85bn).

war_summary: Subsidy intensity peaked in Q3 2025 (heaviest three-way cash burn, mounting regulator pressure on 'involution') and has rolled over since: by Q2 2026 Meituan's core local commerce swung to a RMB5.7bn profit, JD's new-business loss fell to RMB9.85bn from a RMB15.7bn trough, and Alibaba's e-commerce EBITA drag narrowed to near-flat YoY. LatePost/Sina/21jingji coverage frames this as regulators forcing 'anti-involution' discipline plus each player concluding subsidy wars destroy value faster than they build share — Meituan defended share via delivery-network scale and is the only one back to segment profitability, Alibaba held ~42% instant-commerce share while cutting burn, and JD retreated hardest and fastest, trading share for capital discipline.
